content.text: Gold-filled and gold-plated jewellery use different constructions. Gold-filled jewellery has a layer of gold mechanically bonded to a base metal; gold-plated jewellery has gold applied as a surface coating. Neither term means the whole piece is solid gold. Always check both the gold layer and the base metal in the product description.

I Want Jewels describes its gold-coloured pieces as 14kt gold-plated over 925 sterling silver. That is gold-plated sterling silver; the product pages reviewed do not describe these pieces as gold-filled.

content.heading: Gold-filled vs gold-plated at a glance

content.text: The gold layer is only one part of the description. The base metal matters too.

Gold-filled jewellery has a layer of gold mechanically bonded to a base metal. In United States consumer guidance, the Federal Trade Commission distinguishes “gold-filled,” “gold overlay” and “rolled gold plate” from ordinary gold plating and describes the gold layer as mechanically applied.

Gold-filled is not the same as solid gold: the piece still has a base metal beneath the gold layer. Read the full description to see what that base metal is and how the product is marked. Terminology and marking rules can vary by market.

Gold-plated jewellery has a surface layer of gold applied over another material. The base may be sterling silver or a different metal, so “gold-plated” alone does not tell you what the whole piece is made from.
The surface layer can wear over time. Wear depends on factors such as the item’s construction, how often it is worn, friction and care. Check the base metal and finish separately before buying.

content.heading: How to read the product description

items: Base metal: What is the piece mainly made from?
Gold layer or finish: Is the gold solid throughout, mechanically bonded as gold-filled, or applied as plating?
“14kt gold-plated 925 sterling silver” means sterling silver is the base and a 14kt gold layer is the surface finish.
“14kt gold-filled” describes a mechanically bonded layer of 14kt gold over a base metal; check whether the listing identifies that base.
“Solid 14kt gold” means the piece is made throughout from a 14kt gold alloy, rather than just having a gold surface.

content.text: Do not treat “gold colour,” “gold tone” or “gold finish” as proof of the construction. Check the material specification or ask the seller.

content.heading: How I Want Jewels describes its gold-plated pieces

content.text: I Want Jewels’ materials information describes a 925 sterling silver base with 14kt gold plating. For example, the [Amadea Ring](/products/iwjrn0009) lists 925 sterling silver and gold plating.

That means the ring is gold-plated sterling silver, not gold-filled and not solid gold. Check each product page for the specific finish and colour option. The existing [14kt gold-plated jewellery guide](/resources/demi-fine-jewellery-guides/14kt-gold-plated-jewellery-guide) explains the brand’s plated construction in more detail.
Browse the [ring collection](/category/rings), [necklace collection](/category/necklaces) and [earring collection](/category/earrings) for current designs.
Choose based on the complete construction, finish, design and price—not only the word “gold.”

items: Choose gold-filled if you specifically want that construction and the product listing clearly states its base metal and gold details.
Choose gold-plated jewellery if you are comfortable with a gold surface finish over the listed base metal and will follow its care instructions.
Choose solid gold if you want gold throughout the piece and are shopping within that material category.

content.text: There is no one best option for every shopper. Confirm exactly what the product is made from and what its label means in the market where you are buying it.

faq.question: Is gold-filled jewellery solid gold?
faq.answer: No. Gold-filled jewellery has a gold layer mechanically bonded to a base metal. The base metal remains part of the piece.

faq.question: Is gold-filled the same as gold-plated?
faq.answer: No. The terms describe different constructions. Gold-filled uses a mechanically bonded gold layer, while gold-plated jewellery has gold applied as a surface coating.

faq.question: Is 14kt gold-plated sterling silver gold-filled?
faq.answer: No. It describes a sterling silver base with a 14kt gold-plated finish. It should not be called gold-filled unless its actual construction meets that description.

faq.question: Does gold-plated jewellery contain real gold?
faq.answer: The term means gold is applied to the surface, but the full product description should clarify the gold layer and base metal. Check the seller’s specifications.

faq.question: How can I tell whether a piece is gold-filled?
faq.answer: Look for “gold-filled” in the material description and check the karat and base-metal information. In the United States, FTC consumer guidance describes specific terminology and marking expectations; rules may differ in other markets.

faq.question: Does gold plating wear away?
faq.answer: It can wear over time. The rate depends on the piece’s construction, use, friction and care. Follow the seller’s care guidance and see the gold-plated jewellery care guide.
